sn2.7:1.2: The saying by Pañcālacaṇḍa here is quoted by Udāyī and explained by Ānanda at [an9.42](). He makes an appearance at [dn32:10.16](), where he is listed with Āḷavaka, the tutelary deity of Āḷavī, so Pañcālacaṇḍa may be the fierce (_caṇḍa_) protector of the Pañcāla clan. But a Pañcālacaṇḍa appears as a brahmin teacher (Aitereya Āraṇyaka 3.1.6, Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka 7.19, Gopatha Brāhmaṇa 1.1.27n). Perhaps this is that teacher reborn, showing that even this illustrious brahmin of Pañcāla followed the Buddha.
